reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a structured beginner course explaining digital marketing concepts and channels. References to affiliate commissions are framed as educational material, while the enrollment invitation is not shown to require payment, request credentials, guarantee returns, or connect to a harmful mechanism.

citations.quote: DIGITAL MARKETING Full Course for Beginners in 3 Hours | Learn Digital Marketing in 2024

we are starting a basic series of digital marketing, now this is a basic series of digital marketing , so I will not use all the technical words of the first marketing them, we are using it for those small business owners, it is for those people who are starting their career in digital marketing
The main thing is that we do all those efforts in search engine optimization through which our website's ranking will improve regularly in any search engine.
this free digital marketing course will help you acquire essential skills.

opening.argument: The presentation pairs a purportedly free benefit with a direct enrollment action. Viewers are told to “Enroll Now for Digital Marketing Course,” while the description calls it a “free digital marketing course” and supplies a Google Forms enrollment route. That combination is more than neutral information: it presents an easy-to-obtain educational reward and directs the audience into an external registration flow. The title also frames the material as a complete beginner course, increasing the appeal of acting immediately. The solicitation is therefore grounded in the explicit promise of free access linked to enrollment, even though the available material does not establish what happens after registration.

DIGITAL MARKETING Full Course for Beginners in 3 Hours | Learn Digital Marketing in 2024

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a course does not answer the concrete solicitation. The description does not merely discuss digital marketing; it says “Enroll Now” and routes viewers to a form. The absence of a visible payment demand, credential request, or guaranteed return does not make an external registration funnel non-deceptive. The defense establishes subject matter, but it does not establish what the form collects, what access follows, or whether the advertised free benefit is delivered.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The enrollment language is an ordinary way to offer access to educational content, not evidence of a scam. The description explicitly identifies the offer as a free course, and the audio says the series is for small-business owners and people starting careers in digital marketing. Those materials support a genuine instructional purpose. The cited form and “Enroll Now” wording show a registration path, but they do not show payment, credential collection, concealment, or failure to provide the course.

opening.argument: Several low-friction commercial signals appear together. A slide promotes “Entry Resistance is Low” and “High Return on Investment,” while the description advertises a free course, urges enrollment through an external form, and separately offers access to “Premium Videos and Live Streams.” It also provides phone numbers for course information and promotes digital-marketing services. None of these elements alone proves deception, but together they create a funnel built around easy entry, attractive returns, external contact, and additional commercial access. A careful judge should treat that combination as materially riskier than the neutral educational framing suggests, especially because the evidence does not explain the terms of the premium offer or the result of contacting the provider.

citations.quote: this free digital marketing course will help you acquire essential skills.
Get Access to Premium Videos and Live Streams:
For more info about the courses, call us:

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. It points to educational subject matter, but does not explain the slide's “High Return on Investment,” the external enrollment route, or the separate premium-access invitation. The issue is not that the video proves a guaranteed return; it is that low-barrier access and attractive financial framing are placed beside contact and enrollment prompts without disclosed terms. That combination reasonably supports scrutiny of a potentially deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: Enroll Now for Digital Marketing Course
Get Access to Premium Videos and Live Streams:

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited signals do not amount to a scam mechanism. “High Return on Investment” appears as a stated benefit of digital marketing, not a promised payout to viewers, and the description identifies the course as free. Premium videos, a phone contact, and a registration form are ordinary ways an institute can distribute or sell educational material. Nothing in these citations specifies a deposit, guaranteed income, withdrawal, or deceptive outcome.

citations.quote: this free digital marketing course will help you acquire essential skills.
For more info about the courses, call us:

opening.argument: The apparent lesson also functions as promotion for commission-based participation. The affiliate segment defines earning a commission by promoting another company's products, and the speaker describes giving an extra amount when someone purchases through a provided link. The presentation therefore does not merely warn viewers about affiliate marketing; it explains a practical path from contacting influencers and using tracked links to earning money. A slide visibly emphasizes “earning a commission,” reinforcing that income-producing promotion is a featured takeaway. Framed this way, the educational wrapper steers viewers toward recruitment and promotional activity rather than remaining detached instruction.

citations.quote: If someone also purchases from this link then we offer an extra income by giving them the extra amount
you can contact different influencers of your niche then run influencer marketing campaigns as well
you can come in contact with brands or other companies

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the affiliate material educational, but the actual explanation supplies the operational pathway: contact influencers, promote a product, use a link, and receive extra income when a purchase occurs. That is an inducement to recruit promotional participants and drive transactions, not merely a definition. The fact that the segment appears inside a course does not eliminate its promotional effect or establish that the commission arrangement is benign.

citations.quote: If someone also purchases from this link then we offer an extra income by giving them the extra amount
you can contact different influencers of your niche then run influencer marketing campaigns as well

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material describes ordinary affiliate marketing, not a tiered recruitment scheme. It says commissions arise when a customer purchases through a link and explains that influencers promote products to their audiences. It does not show downlines, uplines, matrices, slots, or qualification levels. The lesson's practical detail may explain how affiliate promotion works, but the quotes fail to show that viewers are being recruited into a deceptive commission structure.
